      note: Interpretation amb.2025.mfs_lived_apart: The first, with time in a shared home counted as living together whether or not the spouses were separated (the fourth reading rejected). One question (household.mfs_living) asks when the spouses lived together, with the temporary absence rule and the shared home in its help, and every test reads it. The 6-month rule's statement of temporary absences is the only one the archived text gives, and p501 p. 9 states the same rule for living in the home generally; applying it to the all-year test asks one fact once (norm N8). The EIC's special rule (p. 44) states the separated-spouse test as living apart for the last 6 months, so a spouse who lived with the filer at some time in those months fails it; the third reading would let that filer pass question 4 while failing the rule the question applies. The archived 6-month tests are stated by the home ("lived in the home", "didn’t live in your home"), so spouses under one roof did not live apart for them; reading the all-year test the same way asks one fact once, and the fourth reading would need a second question on estrangement that no source defines. (i1040gi, p. 15, Married persons who live apart, "Temporary absences for special circumstances, such as for business, medical care, school, or military service, count as time lived in the home"; p. 44, Special rule for separated spouses, "You lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025"; p501 p. 8, Considered Unmarried, "Your spouse didn't live in your home during the last 6 months of the tax year")

      note: Interpretation amb.2025.f1116_itemized: The first (f1116.itemized_unread narrowed to Schedule A line 5a; f1116.line3a_itemized unchanged). The regulation, archived now, places the charitable deduction on U.S. income for every filer whose gift is allowed by section 170; the second reading follows Pub. 514's general list, which the regulation displaces. A gift allowed only by a treaty (to a Canadian, Mexican or Israeli charity) is apportioned by income from that country under (e)(12)(ii), which this reading does not catch; it is recorded here as the residue. Gambling losses are deductible only up to gambling winnings and are incurred in the activity that produces them; a foreign gambling winning is not passive income and refuses at ftc.all_passive. Pub. 514 makes the state tax rule depend on "the total income taxed by the state" against U.S. source income, and on whether the state exempts foreign income; neither is on the return, and the split of a capped line 5e between line 2 and line 3a is not stated, so the third reading is rejected and the refusal stays.

Pub. 550: "You can carry over the amount of investment interest you could not deduct because of this limit to the next tax year. The interest carried over is treated as investment interest paid or accrued in that next year." The third reading carries the whole earlier amount past a year whose net investment income could have absorbed it, so it can overstate line 2; it is not used. The second follows the quoted rule but asks the filer to complete a form for a past year. The first can understate the deduction, for a filer whose 2024 net investment income did not absorb the carryforward; it cannot overstate it. (p550, p. 47, Limit on Deduction, "You can carry over the amount of investment interest you could not deduct because of this limit to the next tax year. The interest carried over is treated as investment interest paid or accrued in that next year.")

The same ground as amb.2025.hoh_community_property (owner decision of 2026-10-22, integrity plan decision 10): the community income split of Pub. 555 is outside the tool. "Lived in" is broader than "domicile": a filer who lived in one of the states only temporarily is refused too, which errs toward refusing (settled as design decision D1 of the married-filing-separately scout, by the coordinator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-15). The permanent-home clause and the question on the husband or wife cover the other side: a filer domiciled in one of the states who lived elsewhere (Pub. 555 makes active military pay earned while domiciled there community income, p. 6), and spouses with different domiciles, whose income Pub. 555 settles by the law of each (p. 2), which the tool cannot apply. The question on the husband or wife is not asked after a marriage that ended in 2025 (single or unmarried head of household): one step for about 14% of returns against a very rare case (coordinator, 2026-11-16). Such a return, where only the former husband or wife lived in or had a permanent home in one of the states, is computed without the split. (p555, p. 2, Domicile, "The law of the state, or the law of the foreign country, where you are domiciled will determine if you have community property, community income, or both. == Form IT-201 (2025), Resident Income Tax Return — New York State and New York City ==
  (question) Were you (and your spouse, on a joint return) a New York State resident for all of 2025: domiciled in New York State, or keeping a permanent place of abode in New York State for substantially all of the year and spending 184 days or more there?

      Answer No if, though domiciled in New York, you kept no permanent place of abode in New York, kept one outside New York all year and spent 30 days or less in New York, or met the 548-day foreign-presence test (Group A or B).

      The 184-day test does not apply to a person in active military service, and undergraduate student housing is not a permanent place of abode for the student living in it; a person domiciled in New York State is a resident either way, unless Group A or B applies.

  (question) Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) make a withdrawal during 2025 from an account under New York's 529 college savings program that is nonqualified for New York?

      A withdrawal is nonqualified for New York unless it was used:
      - for the beneficiary's qualified higher education expenses at an eligible college or other post-secondary institution
      - for the beneficiary's qualified postsecondary credentialing expenses at an eligible educational institution, on or after July 4, 2025
      - to pay principal or interest on a qualified education loan of the beneficiary or the beneficiary's sibling
      - for a rollover to a Roth IRA or to an ABLE account
      - for any purpose, if the withdrawal is the result of the beneficiary's death or disability

      Answer Yes for a withdrawal used for elementary or secondary school tuition, or for a transfer to another state's 529 program: New York treats these as nonqualified although they are qualified federally. A transfer between family members' accounts within New York's program, not paid out, is not a withdrawal.

(Form IT-201-I (2025), Instructions for Form IT-201 (including instructions for Forms IT-195 and IT-201-ATT), 41 pages; final 2025 edition; PDF modified 2025-11-20; 29489d6e)
      note: Interpretation amb.ny.2025.whole_dollars: Round each federal amount half-up to the dollar as it is entered on lines 1 to 18, and each computed tax, credit or worksheet line half-up to the dollar where it is computed. Owner decision C4 (docs/ny/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04). The instructions require every entry on the return and its worksheets to be a whole dollar and give the half-up rule; rounding where a line is entered is the literal reading. Rounding lines 1 to 18 separately can make line 19 differ by a few dollars from federal AGI rounded once; ny_it201.line19_agrees shows whether they agree. Rounding can explain at most $8 (lines 1 to 11, 13 to 16 and 18 are 16 entries, each rounded by at most 50 cents), so ny_it201.gate.line19_gap refuses a line 19 more than $8 from federal adjusted gross income rounded once: such a gap means a federal amount reached federal adjusted gross income without reaching lines 1 to 18 (the tolerance chosen under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-23). A product of a rate and an amount is rounded once to the dollar (multiply_rate with unit 100), not first to the cent. A negative amount ending in exactly 50 cents (a loss carried from federal lines 5, 6, 7, 8 or 11 in cents, for example -$213.50) is increased to the next dollar toward zero (-$213): the engine's half-up rule, floor(x + 1/2). Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (BUG-1220). The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.
 (ny_it201i, p. 2, Entering whole dollar amounts, "When you enter amounts on your return, enter whole dollar amounts only.")

The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.

Rounding lines 1 to 18 separately can make line 19 differ by a few dollars from federal AGI rounded once; ny_it201.line19_agrees shows whether they agree. Rounding can explain at most $8 (lines 1 to 11, 13 to 16 and 18 are 16 entries, each rounded by at most 50 cents), so ny_it201.gate.line19_gap refuses a line 19 more than $8 from federal adjusted gross income rounded once: such a gap means a federal amount reached federal adjusted gross income without reaching lines 1 to 18 (the tolerance chosen under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-23). A product of a rate and an amount is rounded once to the dollar (multiply_rate with unit 100), not first to the cent. A negative amount ending in exactly 50 cents (a loss carried from federal lines 5, 6, 7, 8 or 11 in cents, for example -$213.50) is increased to the next dollar toward zero (-$213): the engine's half-up rule, floor(x + 1/2). Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (BUG-1220). The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.

The gate also refuses, without testing each business, a person with two or more businesses that have employees and a profit.       = UNKNOWN (no input supplied for ny_it201.ask.city_resident)
      cite: [ny_it201i-html] Tax computation worksheet 6, "Multiply line 1 by 10.9% (0.109)" (Web edition of Form IT-201-I (2025) ('2025 Form IT-201-I, Instructions for Form IT-201'); page 'Updated: July 27, 2026'. Every number of the PDF edition occurs in it and every word of every PDF page bar the six excepted pages (check_extraction.py --jurisdiction ny); b866b238)
      note: Interpretation amb.ny.2025.whole_dollars: Round each federal amount half-up to the dollar as it is entered on lines 1 to 18, and each computed tax, credit or worksheet line half-up to the dollar where it is computed. Owner decision C4 (docs/ny/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04). The instructions require every entry on the return and its worksheets to be a whole dollar and give the half-up rule; rounding where a line is entered is the literal reading. Rounding lines 1 to 18 separately can make line 19 differ by a few dollars from federal AGI rounded once; ny_it201.line19_agrees shows whether they agree. Rounding can explain at most $8 (lines 1 to 11, 13 to 16 and 18 are 16 entries, each rounded by at most 50 cents), so ny_it201.gate.line19_gap refuses a line 19 more than $8 from federal adjusted gross income rounded once: such a gap means a federal amount reached federal adjusted gross income without reaching lines 1 to 18 (the tolerance chosen under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-23). A product of a rate and an amount is rounded once to the dollar (multiply_rate with unit 100), not first to the cent. A negative amount ending in exactly 50 cents (a loss carried from federal lines 5, 6, 7, 8 or 11 in cents, for example -$213.50) is increased to the next dollar toward zero (-$213): the engine's half-up rule, floor(x + 1/2). Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (BUG-1220). The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.
 (ny_it201i, p. 2, Entering whole dollar amounts, "When you enter amounts on your return, enter whole dollar amounts only.")

      note: guard incomplete; possible: #0 unknown, #1 unknown, #2 unknown, #3 unknown, #4 unknown, none unknown; Interpretation amb.ny.2025.recapture_selection: Taxable income selects the Recapture Base, Incremental Benefit and the amount the excess of New York AGI is measured over; New York AGI only gates the worksheets (more than $107,650; more than $25,000,000 is the flat 10.9%) and measures the phase-in (the worksheets' conditions). Tax Law § 601(d-4) (ny_tax_law_601, the 2025-07-11 revision, for "taxable years beginning on or after two thousand twenty-three and before two thousand twenty-six") is the first reading, for every filing status. For resident unmarried individuals and married individuals filing separately, (d-4)(3)(A): "If New York adjusted gross income is greater than $107,650, but not over $25,000,000: (i) the recapture base and incremental benefit shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:" (rows greater than $80,650 not over $215,400, $0 and $568; greater than $215,400 not over $1,077,550, $568 and $1,831; to $5,000,000, $2,399 and $30,172; to $25,000,000, $32,571 and $32,500), and "(ii) the applicable amount shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:" (greater than $80,650 not over $215,400, "New York adjusted gross income minus $107,650"; greater than $215,400 not over $1,077,550, "New York adjusted gross income minus $215,400"; and so on); the supplemental tax is the recapture base plus the incremental benefit times the lesser of $50,000 or the applicable amount over $50,000. Paragraph (1) (joint returns and surviving spouses; taxable-income rows from $27,900, $161,550, $323,200, $2,155,350, $5,000,000; amounts $333/$807, $1,140/$2,747, $3,887/$60,350, $64,237/$32,500) and paragraph (2) (heads of households; rows from $107,650, $269,300, $1,616,450, $5,000,000; amounts $787/$2,289, $3,076/$45,261, $48,337/$32,500) have the same form. Below the first row the proviso takes the flat rate (5.50% joint, 6.00% the others) times taxable income less the table tax, times the lesser of $50,000 or New York AGI minus $107,650 over $50,000, which is worksheets 1, 7 and 12; above $25,000,000 of New York AGI, 10.90% of taxable income (worksheets 6, 11 and 16). Every amount and threshold the worksheets print (params/ny/2025.yaml ny.tcw.*) equals the statute's. The worksheets' extra New York AGI floor on worksheets 2 onward (for example "more than $215,400" on worksheet 8) is implied by the taxable-income test, since taxable income is not more than New York AGI. Two differences are immaterial here: the statute's rows ("greater than $80,650") and proviso ("less than eighty thousand six hundred fifty dollars") both leave out taxable income of exactly $80,650 (and $27,900, $107,650), where the two formulas give the same amount; and the statute's fraction is not rounded, the worksheets' is, to four places (amb.ny.2025.fourth_decimal). Owner decision 2026-11-04: follow the statute; the statute and the instructions agree, so the differential cases are PolicyEngine-US's departure from both.

      note: Interpretation amb.ny.2025.whole_dollars: Round each federal amount half-up to the dollar as it is entered on lines 1 to 18, and each computed tax, credit or worksheet line half-up to the dollar where it is computed. Owner decision C4 (docs/ny/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04). The instructions require every entry on the return and its worksheets to be a whole dollar and give the half-up rule; rounding where a line is entered is the literal reading. Rounding lines 1 to 18 separately can make line 19 differ by a few dollars from federal AGI rounded once; ny_it201.line19_agrees shows whether they agree. Rounding can explain at most $8 (lines 1 to 11, 13 to 16 and 18 are 16 entries, each rounded by at most 50 cents), so ny_it201.gate.line19_gap refuses a line 19 more than $8 from federal adjusted gross income rounded once: such a gap means a federal amount reached federal adjusted gross income without reaching lines 1 to 18 (the tolerance chosen under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-23). A product of a rate and an amount is rounded once to the dollar (multiply_rate with unit 100), not first to the cent. A negative amount ending in exactly 50 cents (a loss carried from federal lines 5, 6, 7, 8 or 11 in cents, for example -$213.50) is increased to the next dollar toward zero (-$213): the engine's half-up rule, floor(x + 1/2). Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (BUG-1220). The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.

  1   Maximum amount
      = $2,500,000
      cite: [i4562] p. 4, Line 1, "Generally, the maximum section 179 expense deduction is $2,500,000 for section 179 property ... placed in service during the tax year beginning in 2025" (2025; 5c1c95b7)
      note: Interpretation amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property: The second. s179.line1 is the $2,500,000 the line 1 instruction states, so line 5 is the dollar limitation and a carryover is deducted up to the dollar limitation less the 2025 election and up to the business income limit (line 11). On a separate return line 5 is 50% of the limitation, the instruction's allocation when the spouses elect no other. Research for the owner (ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md) quotes the archived 26 U.S.C. 179(b)(3)(B), Treas. Reg. 1.179-2(b) and 1.179-3(b) to (d), and P.L. 119-21 sec. 70306. The carryover's room is "the limitation of paragraphs (1) and (2)", the dollar amount, which the cost of 2025 property reduces only above $4,000,000. Form 4562 computes exactly that when line 1 is the $2,500,000 the line 1 instruction states (p. 4). The optional Worksheet 1 instead takes the smaller of that and the cost of 2025 property, a cap that changes no return without a carryover and departs from the statute on a return with one. (i4562, p. 4, Line 1 and Worksheet 1; p. 5, Line 5)

      note: Interpretation amb.2025.rental_not_qbi: The first. Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (lane rentals, BUG-1148), replacing the reading of 2026-11-15 (a rental is not a trade or business unless the filer says it is). Trade or business status is a fact, not an election, and a rental that is one must be counted in QBI; under the second reading a filer who never claimed it answers No and a rental loss is left out of QBI, overstating the deduction (understating tax). The first refuses more landlords who think of their rental as a business. Rev. Proc. 2019-38 is not archived. To reverse: restore the claim wording of sche.qbi_business's source and bank entry. (i8995, p. 1, Trade or business, "an activity qualifies as a trade or business if your primary purpose for engaging in the activity is for income or profit and you’re involved in the activity with continuity and regularity" and "provides a safe harbor under which a rental real estate enterprise will be treated as a trade or business for purposes of the QBI deduction")

Interpretation amb.2025.s1_nol_limit_test: The first (s1.nol_ti, s1.nol_ti4, s1.nol_limit_test, refused at f1040.line15 by s1.nol_limit). Checked against the forms (lane x2-s1o, 2026-11-15): the above-the-line deductions with phase-outs (student loan interest, IRA) fall as modified AGI rises; taxable social security benefits rise with other income, so AGI without the NOL is at least AGI with it plus N; the itemized deductions with an AGI floor (medical, casualty) and the SALT limit that falls above $500,000 of modified AGI fall as AGI rises; the larger of itemized and standard deductions keeps that direction; Schedule 1-A deductions (tips, overtime, car loan interest, seniors) phase out with modified AGI; the QBI deduction is left out of T0 and only lowers T. Interpretation amb.2025.f1116_itemized: The first (f1116.itemized_unread narrowed to Schedule A line 5a; f1116.line3a_itemized unchanged). The regulation, archived now, places the charitable deduction on U.S. income for every filer whose gift is allowed by section 170; the second reading follows Pub. 514's general list, which the regulation displaces. A gift allowed only by a treaty (to a Canadian, Mexican or Israeli charity) is apportioned by income from that country under (e)(12)(ii), which this reading does not catch; it is recorded here as the residue. Gambling losses are deductible only up to gambling winnings and are incurred in the activity that produces them; a foreign gambling winning is not passive income and refuses at ftc.all_passive. Pub. 514 makes the state tax rule depend on "the total income taxed by the state" against U.S. source income, and on whether the state exempts foreign income; neither is on the return, and the split of a capped line 5e between line 2 and line 3a is not stated, so the third reading is rejected and the refusal stays.
 (p514, p. 27, State income taxes; Deductions not definitely related)

 (i1116, p. 18, Lines 4a and 4b)

Interpretation amb.2025.f1116_high_taxed: The first (f1116col.div_hi, f1116col.int_hi and the group lines; f1116.high_taxed when either group's tax is more than 37 percent of its income after deductions, refused on line 35). The regulation fixes the rate as the highest rate "specified in section 1", 37 percent for 2025, and (c)(2)(iii) makes the test before the section 904(b) adjustments, which is where qualified dividends get their lower rate; so the third reading is rejected. The return holds income and tax per column and kind, not per payment: a fund reports one foreign tax on one foreign income, and a country's treaty rate is normally one rate, so the per column and kind ratio is the payment's rate in the common cases. Every deduction on the returns computed (line 3c and home mortgage interest) is apportioned by gross income, so each group bears the same share of them; a group can be a loss only when all are, so the reallocation of (c)(2)(ii) never moves income between groups here. The residue is a column whose payments straddle 15 percent, classed by its average.
 (cfr-26-1-904-4, p. 3, (c) High-taxed income; p. 4, (c)(2) and (c)(3))

Interpretation amb.ny.2025.whole_dollars: Round each federal amount half-up to the dollar as it is entered on lines 1 to 18, and each computed tax, credit or worksheet line half-up to the dollar where it is computed. Owner decision C4 (docs/ny/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04). The instructions require every entry on the return and its worksheets to be a whole dollar and give the half-up rule; rounding where a line is entered is the literal reading. Rounding lines 1 to 18 separately can make line 19 differ by a few dollars from federal AGI rounded once; ny_it201.line19_agrees shows whether they agree. Rounding can explain at most $8 (lines 1 to 11, 13 to 16 and 18 are 16 entries, each rounded by at most 50 cents), so ny_it201.gate.line19_gap refuses a line 19 more than $8 from federal adjusted gross income rounded once: such a gap means a federal amount reached federal adjusted gross income without reaching lines 1 to 18 (the tolerance chosen under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-23). A product of a rate and an amount is rounded once to the dollar (multiply_rate with unit 100), not first to the cent. A negative amount ending in exactly 50 cents (a loss carried from federal lines 5, 6, 7, 8 or 11 in cents, for example -$213.50) is increased to the next dollar toward zero (-$213): the engine's half-up rule, floor(x + 1/2). Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (BUG-1220). The instructions are silent on the direction for a loss: "Increase amounts that are 50 cents or more to the next dollar" read literally raises -$213.50 to -$213, while "place a minus sign immediately to the left of the loss amount" (p. 3) can be read as rounding the loss's magnitude first (-$214). The first is taken because it is the literal "increase" and, where the text is silent, it does not understate tax (the smaller loss). The alternative, rounding the magnitude half away from zero, would change at most $1 on each of lines 2, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 16 (and so line 17) and is reversed by giving the engine's round a rule that rounds a negative amount's magnitude, with tools/ny_predict.py r_dollar changed to match and fixture ny.whole_dollars.loss_half restated.
 (ny_it201i, p. 2, Entering whole dollar amounts, "When you enter amounts on your return, enter whole dollar amounts only.")
Interpretation amb.ny.2025.item_c: Ask item C as a New York question of its own, in New York's words. Owner decision B8 (docs/ny/DECISIONS.md). (ny_it201i, p. 5, Item C, "You must mark the Yes box even if the other taxpayer did not claim you as a dependent.")
Interpretation amb.2025.rental_not_qbi: The first. Decided by the coordinator under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-24 (lane rentals, BUG-1148), replacing the reading of 2026-11-15 (a rental is not a trade or business unless the filer says it is). Trade or business status is a fact, not an election, and a rental that is one must be counted in QBI; under the second reading a filer who never claimed it answers No and a rental loss is left out of QBI, overstating the deduction (understating tax). The first refuses more landlords who think of their rental as a business. Rev. Proc. 2019-38 is not archived. To reverse: restore the claim wording of sche.qbi_business's source and bank entry. (i8995, p. 1, Trade or business, "an activity qualifies as a trade or business if your primary purpose for engaging in the activity is for income or profit and you’re involved in the activity with continuity and regularity" and "provides a safe harbor under which a rental real estate enterprise will be treated as a trade or business for purposes of the QBI deduction")
Interpretation amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property: The second. s179.line1 is the $2,500,000 the line 1 instruction states, so line 5 is the dollar limitation and a carryover is deducted up to the dollar limitation less the 2025 election and up to the business income limit (line 11). On a separate return line 5 is 50% of the limitation, the instruction's allocation when the spouses elect no other. Research for the owner (ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md) quotes the archived 26 U.S.C. 179(b)(3)(B), Treas. Reg. 1.179-2(b) and 1.179-3(b) to (d), and P.L. 119-21 sec. 70306. The carryover's room is "the limitation of paragraphs (1) and (2)", the dollar amount, which the cost of 2025 property reduces only above $4,000,000. Form 4562 computes exactly that when line 1 is the $2,500,000 the line 1 instruction states (p. 4). The optional Worksheet 1 instead takes the smaller of that and the cost of 2025 property, a cap that changes no return without a carryover and departs from the statute on a return with one. (i4562, p. 4, Line 1 and Worksheet 1; p. 5, Line 5)

Interpretation amb.ny.2025.fourth_decimal: Round the ratio half-up at the fourth decimal place. "Round" without a direction is read as ordinary half-up rounding, the reading the federal register takes for the same instruction on the Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet (amb.2025.sli_ratio_places). The product of the ratio and the whole-dollar amount is rounded once, half-up, to the dollar: the amount is scaled by 100 so that prorate's product is exact, and the scaled product is divided by 100 with one rounding (an earlier version rounded to the cent first, which the in-session review found gave $1 too much on some returns).
 (ny_it201i-html, Tax computation worksheet 1, "7. Divide line 6 by $50,000 and round the result to the fourth decimal place")
Interpretation amb.ny.2025.recapture_selection: Taxable income selects the Recapture Base, Incremental Benefit and the amount the excess of New York AGI is measured over; New York AGI only gates the worksheets (more than $107,650; more than $25,000,000 is the flat 10.9%) and measures the phase-in (the worksheets' conditions). Tax Law § 601(d-4) (ny_tax_law_601, the 2025-07-11 revision, for "taxable years beginning on or after two thousand twenty-three and before two thousand twenty-six") is the first reading, for every filing status. For resident unmarried individuals and married individuals filing separately, (d-4)(3)(A): "If New York adjusted gross income is greater than $107,650, but not over $25,000,000: (i) the recapture base and incremental benefit shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:" (rows greater than $80,650 not over $215,400, $0 and $568; greater than $215,400 not over $1,077,550, $568 and $1,831; to $5,000,000, $2,399 and $30,172; to $25,000,000, $32,571 and $32,500), and "(ii) the applicable amount shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:" (greater than $80,650 not over $215,400, "New York adjusted gross income minus $107,650"; greater than $215,400 not over $1,077,550, "New York adjusted gross income minus $215,400"; and so on); the supplemental tax is the recapture base plus the incremental benefit times the lesser of $50,000 or the applicable amount over $50,000. Paragraph (1) (joint returns and surviving spouses; taxable-income rows from $27,900, $161,550, $323,200, $2,155,350, $5,000,000; amounts $333/$807, $1,140/$2,747, $3,887/$60,350, $64,237/$32,500) and paragraph (2) (heads of households; rows from $107,650, $269,300, $1,616,450, $5,000,000; amounts $787/$2,289, $3,076/$45,261, $48,337/$32,500) have the same form. Below the first row the proviso takes the flat rate (5.50% joint, 6.00% the others) times taxable income less the table tax, times the lesser of $50,000 or New York AGI minus $107,650 over $50,000, which is worksheets 1, 7 and 12; above $25,000,000 of New York AGI, 10.90% of taxable income (worksheets 6, 11 and 16). Every amount and threshold the worksheets print (params/ny/2025.yaml ny.tcw.*) equals the statute's. The worksheets' extra New York AGI floor on worksheets 2 onward (for example "more than $215,400" on worksheet 8) is implied by the taxable-income test, since taxable income is not more than New York AGI. Two differences are immaterial here: the statute's rows ("greater than $80,650") and proviso ("less than eighty thousand six hundred fifty dollars") both leave out taxable income of exactly $80,650 (and $27,900, $107,650), where the two formulas give the same amount; and the statute's fraction is not rounded, the worksheets' is, to four places (amb.ny.2025.fourth_decimal). Owner decision 2026-11-04: follow the statute; the statute and the instructions agree, so the differential cases are PolicyEngine-US's departure from both.
 (ny_tax_law_601, § 601(d-4)(3)(A), "(i) the recapture base and incremental benefit shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:", "(ii) the applicable amount shall be determined by New York taxable income as follows:")

Interpretation amb.2025.refund_exceptions: The first (refund.box8 and refund.not_prior_year on refund.taxable; refund.exc_tax and refund.exc_who on refund.line1; refund.other on Schedule 1 line 1). The TIP is stated for "the year you paid the tax", which is 2024 only when the refund is for 2024 and was paid then, so items 1 and 5 can make a refund taxable even when you did not itemize for 2024, and a part of the refund for a 2025 payment changes the 2025 deduction for taxes (Pub. 525 p. 24, Example 28). A 2024 refund of tax paid before 2024 is a recovery for the year in which the tax was paid (Pub. 525 p. 24, Recovery for 2 or more years), so it is asked with item 5 and refused by refund.not_prior_year. Items 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and the nonresident rule change only how much of a refund of a deducted tax is included; when no income tax was deducted for 2024, none is (Pub. 525 p. 24, Deductions not itemized). Box 8 sends a taxable refund to Schedule C or F whatever the itemizing. A recovery deducted on an earlier Form 8960 is refused by f8960.refund when Form 8960 is filed (modified AGI above the threshold); below the threshold it changes no amount. (i1040gi, pp. 88–89, Line 1, "Exception. See Itemized Deduction Recoveries in Pub. 525 instead of using the State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet"; p525 p. 24, Deductions not itemized)
Interpretation amb.2025.refund_two_returns: The first (refund.two_returns, refund.two_itemized, refund.worksheet, and the refusal on refund.taxable). The worksheet is written for one 2024 return, and a recovery is included only to the extent the deduction reduced the tax of the year in which it was taken (Pub. 525 p. 24, Itemized Deduction Recoveries), so a refund belongs with the return on which its tax was deducted. The instructions do not say how to combine two 2024 returns. The second reading is the likely method, but it is arithmetic the instructions do not print, and it doubles the worksheet's questions for a rare case. The third can be wrong in either direction (BUG-0593). When neither 2024 return deducted state and local income taxes, the TIP on p. 88 makes the answer zero whichever return is meant, so it is not refused. (i1040gi, p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet—Schedule 1, Line 1, line 1, "But don’t enter more than the amount of your state and local income taxes shown on your 2024 Schedule A, line 5d"; p. 88, Line 1, "None of your refund is taxable if, in the year you paid the tax")

Interpretation amb.2025.sa_dep_earned: The printed formula over the return's lines (sa.dep_earned). Lines 6, 8t and 8u are refused before this worksheet is reached (Schedule F, and Schedule 1 lines 8t and 8u through s1.line8_other), so only lines 1z, 3, 8r and 15 enter it. On a joint return the lines hold both spouses' amounts. A total below zero is entered as zero (Pub. 501 Table 8, line 1, "If none, enter -0-"), which leaves line 2 unchanged: any earned income of $900 or less gives $1,350. Line 2 is figured as the larger of earned income plus $450 and $1,350 (Pub. 501 p. 24, "the greater of"), the same amount as the worksheet's Yes and No.
 The worksheet gives the formula for the lines a filer has in hand, and Pub. 501 Example 4 applies it with a business loss reducing earned income ($7,000 of wages less a $3,000 loss, $4,000). Line 1z can hold amounts that are not plainly pay for services (taxable employer-provided adoption benefits, line 1f); the formula counts them as written, and the word "Generally" is read as covering them. The joint-return reading is the worksheet's own: line 3 prints the joint amount and line 1 counts both spouses' boxes, and it says "your earned income" of a return whose lines are combined. A joint return where only one spouse is claimable and both have earned income may read differently; no archived text settles it.
 (i1040gi, p. 35, Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents—Line 12e, note to line 2)

Interpretation amb.2025.sep_loss_floor: The second. A maximum deductible contribution below zero has no meaning, and the first reading would make a zero contribution exceed it, refusing every return with a SEP plan and a Schedule C loss at person.sep_excess. On the second, a zero contribution deducts zero and any contribution above zero is refused as excess, which is the deduction the first reading gives wherever it gives one. Where both readings complete the return, no Form 1040 or Schedule 1 amount differs; only the printed worksheet steps do (BUG-0180, regression stage14.sep.loss_floor). (p560, p. 39, chapter 5, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, Step 3, "Subtract step 2 from step 1", and Step 21, "This is your maximum deductible contribution")
Interpretation amb.2025.sep_rate_places: Six decimal places, half-up (person.sep_s5); only whole-percent plan rates are accepted, which the Rate Table covers. For whole-percent plan rates the Rate Table applies, and it prints six places; "at least 3" permits six. (p560, chapter 5, Rate Table for Self-Employed and Rate Worksheet for Self-Employed)
Interpretation amb.2025.savers_sep_contrib: The first (person.sav_simple_plan). The owner's decision (Stage 15 premise map, decision 2). Only elective deferrals to a SEP (code F, a salary reduction SEP) are named; a SEP contribution a self-employed person makes for themselves is a nonelective contribution. (f8880, p. 2, Line 2, "Elective deferrals (including designated Roth contributions under section 402A, if applicable) to a 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457(b), SEP, SIMPLE, or the federal TSP")
Interpretation amb.2025.ira_line7_cents: The first. The project's rule for products (amb.2025.multiplication_subcent). The readings differ only when the exact product is less than half a cent above a multiple of $10. (i1040gi, p. 98, IRA Deduction Worksheet—Continued, line 7, "If the result isn’t a multiple of $10, increase it to the next multiple of $10 (for example, increase $490.30 to $500)")
Interpretation amb.2025.edu_1098t_date: The first, in the help text of person.edu_1098t and dependent.edu_1098t. Pub. 970 is the later revision and explains the shift (January 31 falls on a Saturday). Owner's decision D7(d), 2026-10-29. (p970, p. 2, Reminders, "After February 2, 2026 (January 31 falls on a Saturday), but before you file your 2025 tax return, you or the student must request that the educational institution furnish Form 1098-T.")
Interpretation amb.2025.edu_filer_tin: The first; without it an American opportunity credit student goes to the lifetime learning credit (line 31). Both spouses are filers of a joint return, and the text says "Filers". The 2026 draft instructions read one spouse as enough, but under the new valid-SSN rule of P.L. 119-21 sec. 70606, which is not the 2025 text. Owner's decision D7(a), 2026-10-29. (i8863, p. 3, Student qualifications, "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions).")
Interpretation amb.2025.edu_fulltime: The first (person.edu_fulltime asks the 5-month definition). Condition 1c points to "(defined later)", and the only definition later is the 5-month one. Owner's decision D7(c), 2026-10-29. (i8863, p. 7, Full-time student, "you were a full-time student for 2025 if during any part of any 5 calendar months during the year you were enrolled as a full-time student at an eligible educational institution (defined earlier)")
Interpretation amb.2025.f5329_birth_cap: The first (person.x_cap19 is $5,000 times the number of births or adoptions). The instructions tie the amount to each birth or adoption, and the publication to each taxpayer; the statute (26 U.S.C. 72(t)(2)(H)) is to be archived as a second printing. Owner's decision D8(c), 2026-10-29. (p590b, p. 28, Qualified birth or adoption distribution, "A qualified birth or adoption distribution must not exceed $5,000 per taxpayer.")
Scope: Form 1040 lines 1a–37 with the schedules and forms this tool implements and their refusal screens. Unsupported paths are refused with citations. No filing or transmission.
Rounding: amounts are exact cents; the return-wide whole-dollar rounding setting is deferred (see ambiguities/2025.yaml).
Estimated tax penalty: not computed. The IRS generally figures it and sends a bill (i1040gi, line 38; i2210, Who Must File Form 2210). You must file Form 2210 yourself to ask for a waiver, to use the annualized income installment method or the dates tax was actually withheld (Form 2210, Part II, boxes A to D), or if you filed a joint return for 2024 or 2025 but not both and the payment based on your 2024 tax (Form 2210, line 8) is smaller than 90% of your 2025 tax (line 5) (box E).
Refund: lines 35b to 35d are not asked. If line 34 shows a refund, give your routing number, account number and account type on lines 35b to 35d, or attach Form 8888 to split it; from October 2025 the IRS generally stopped issuing paper refund checks (i1040gi, Line 35a, p. 62).
This is a computation of published IRS forms and instructions; it is not tax or legal advice. Published instructions are not the law itself.
